summary: Plan validates and covers D1-D10 with disjoint parallel ownership and a sound holdout design, but docs ordering, post-tuning regression checks and the lack of an agent-spend budget need fixing before approval.

criteria.description: Every D-criterion (D1-D10) maps to a task with acceptance criteria and a verification command
Parallel tasks have disjoint file ownership; no gaps; dependency order is acyclic and matches data flow
Holdout protection: manifest, run cap, authored by test-engineer, excluded from BE/AI, procedural controls disclosed
Docs/D9/D10 reflect the final state of the code and eval results
Cost realism against the remaining harness budget (about 56 USD)

findings.title: docs-devops does not depend on live-eval
findings.detail: docs-devops depends only on browser-e2e, so it can run in parallel with live-eval. The README must contain measured eval results and cost rules, and the clean-checkout npm test must run after live-eval changes src/ai/prompt.js, src/ai/fallback.js and src/verify/stopwords.js. The critical path in plan.md also ends live-eval -> docs, contradicting the task graph.
findings.recommendation: Add live-eval to docs-devops dependencies. Resolved when plan.json shows it and plan validate passes.

findings.title: No regression check after tuning edits; live-eval verification is only test:live
findings.detail: live-eval modifies prompt.js, fallback.js and stopwords.js (built earlier by ai-providers and verifier-notes) after the unit, API, eval and browser suites passed, yet its verification command is only npm run test:live. Stoplist or fallback changes can break M1b/M1c, fallback-tune, determinism and browser fixtures.
findings.recommendation: Require npm test and npm run test:browser green after the last tuning change (acceptance criterion or verification command), plus M1b 100% and M1c <=2% re-run. Note that stopwords.js is backend-owned in spec section 11 and edits go through the tuning log.

findings.title: No agent-spend budget; live-eval allowances are unrealistic for the remaining harness budget
findings.detail: The plan has 13 tasks, 8 phase gates and a verification gate but no estimate of agent spend. It relies on the spec figures of a 3 USD per-run cap and a 40 USD aggregate live-eval budget (8 tune runs plus holdout), about 70 percent of the roughly 56 USD remaining. The spec estimates real runs at 0.7-2.0 USD and calls the estimates unmeasured. An overrun would halt delivery before docs and verification.
findings.recommendation: Add a budget table to plan.md: expected agent spend per phase, and a live-eval aggregate cap that fits (suggest <=12 USD, <=4 tune runs, per-run cap 1.5 USD, stop-and-report rule at 70 percent of the harness budget). Reflect it in live-eval acceptance criteria.

findings.title: Frontend phase verification is only node --check
findings.detail: D1 criteria (overflow, focus, touch targets, states) are untested until browser-e2e, so the frontend phase gate verifies little. test/support/mock-api.js is produced but nothing exercises it.
findings.recommendation: Either state that D1 evidence is deferred to tests-e2e, or add a small node:test asserting every spec 7.3 data-testid exists in public/.

findings.title: Holdout run-count inconsistency
findings.detail: plan.md risks say holdout 2 per provider, live-eval criteria say one run each. The spec says cap 2, second only for a harness defect.
findings.recommendation: State one run each, a second only after a harness defect and disclosed.

findings.title: Holdout read restriction is procedural; lessonDecisions empty
findings.detail: The restriction on backend and AI reading eval/holdout is policy plus manifest, run log and git-history review, as the spec states openly. Memory has no records, so empty lessonDecisions is acceptable.
findings.recommendation: No change required; keep the git-history inspection in the verification gate.
